newsitem.title: GREECE: Banks lead 0.58pct correction in Greek shares.
newsitem.headline: Banks lead 0.58pct correction in Greek shares.

text.p: Greek shares were trading lower in early Friday dealing in what was seen by analysts as a short-term correction that will produce underlying support.
The Athens general index was off 0.58 percent or 9.56 points to 1,633.95 from Thursday's close of 1,643.51 after 30 minutes of trading.
Banks were leading the market lower with a 1.19 percent drop.
Analysts said the market was at a turning point due to the lack of a price correction which would strenghten underlying support.

"The market is entering a critical stage because the market produced a long streak of rising sessions without a pause or short-term correction in order to build up fresh underlying support," said Maria Lentziou, analyst at Olympic Securities.
Price corrections had taken place during intraday trading in previous sessions but did not extend in consecutive days.
"Corrections take place during the course of each session but the net effect is always positive for the index because buyers outstrip sellers towards the end of each session," she said.
There was a clear distinction in the profile of the two sides of the market in recent sessions.
"The buy side is dominated by retail investors while sellers are mostly institutional portfolios realising their capital gains," Lentziou said.
But institutionals plough back their profits and stalk for new opportunities to take new positions at even slightly lower price levels, she added.
The seven year old all-time zenith of 1,684.31 was not seen as a daunting psychological factor to market trends.

"The historic high level does not constitute a target or barrier to the market's momentum. The index penetrated several psychological barriers and resistance levels in the recent past with remarkable ease," said Lentziou.
Turnover amounted to 4.8 billion drachmas on 1.2 million shares traded. Declining stocks beat advancers 105 to 65 with 23 stocks unchanged on 193 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted unchanged at 1,093-1,123. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were flat at 6,545 drachmas.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $85.14-$86.83. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted lower at 3,569-3,792 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $20.65-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.
